question.text: Famous Tang poet Li Bai was born in a town along this trading route from China to the Mediterranean. A particular Chinese fabric gave this trading route its name.
question.clue: A 2015 best-selling history book by Peter Frankopan is titled for the plural form of this entity.

swap.leadin: This group mocked the US, France, and UK forces during a mock funeral in Khost.
swap.text: Name this group that took over a certain country after defeating a resistance movement in Panjshir Province. This group, which takes its name from the word "students," is largely led by Pashtun militants.
swap.clue: This group, the main opponent of the Northern Alliance, carried out the "green on blue" attacks.

question.leadin: This ruler defeated Tokhtamysh [TOKE-TAM-ISH] at the Battle of the Terek River. --.
question.text: Name this conqueror from Samarkand who sacked Damascus and Delhi.
question.clue: This man captured Sultan Bayezid the Thunderbolt at the Battle of Ankara.

swap.leadin: As a child, this person defeated their blood brother Jamukha and rescued their kidnapped wife Borte ["BOHR-tay"] from a rival tribe.
swap.text: Name this person, who ruled the largest contiguous empire in history. This person born with the name Temujin was succeeded by their son Ogedei.
swap.clue: One of his greatest accomplishments was winning the Battle of the Badger Mouth, while another victory saw him ferociously smash the Khwarezmi empire and destroy their capitals of Urgench and Samarkand.

question.leadin: This successor state of the Mongol Empire was defeated by Dmitry Donskoy at the Battle of Kulikovo.
question.text: Name this state, which was allegedly named for the color of Batu Khan's tent. This state's rule over Russia ended after Ivan the Great's victory at the Great Stand on the Ugra River.
question.answerHtml: Golden Horde (accept Blue Horde or White Horde, accept Great Horde, accept Ulug Ulus)
question.clue: Economically centered at Bolgary, its cities also included the capital Sarai.

swap.leadin: The Yassa was an oral law code used by this empire.
swap.text: Name this empire founded by Genghis Khan whose successor states included the Yuan (YOO-un) dynasty.
swap.clue: It used a trebuchet to beat the Southern Song at Xiangyang .

question.leadin: Answer the following about people messing with calendars.
question.text: As president of this country, Sarparmurat Niyazov renamed April "Gurbansoltan"after his mother. Even more hilariously, bread was also renamed Gurbansoltan during Niyazov's rule in this country.
question.clue: The Rukhnama, or "Book of Soul," was a propaganda work written by a former head of this state, Saparmurat Niyazov.

swap.leadin: This empire was formed in the 7th century AD following the end of the Zhangzhung kingdom.
swap.text: Name this ancient Himalayan empire which flourished until the 9th century and had a capital at Lhasa.
swap.clue: Ralpacan was one of this empire's Three Dharma Kings.

question.leadin: Qazi ("kah-zi") Mullah led a state in this mountain range that was invaded during the Murid War.
question.text: Name this mountain range, where the Naqshbandi Sufi leader Imam Shamil led resistance to foreign occupation. The Circassian ethnic group is from this mountain range.
question.clue: Bagrationi Dynasty rulers such as Tamar the Great led a kingdom based in this range.The Circassians were based in this range, near the site of a genocide that remains ignored underArticle 301 today.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a certain country.
swap.text: Its first namesake war against the British occurred in 1838 when Dost Muhammad was deposed and then restored after a revolution in Kabul.
swap.clue: In 1977 Loya Jirga secured one party rule under the National Revolutionary Party under a President who was the cousin of former king Mohammad Zahir Shah.

question.leadin: NATO operations in this province were often organised from the Main Operating Base in Lashkar Gah.
question.text: Identify this province. American and British troops combating the Taliban were stationed at Camp Leatherneck and Camp Bastion in this province.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the history of a mountainous nation that's been in the news a lot.
swap.text: In 1893, the British set up this border between Afghanistan and Pakistan based on geographical features, not ethnic regions. This idiotic idea continues to lend itself today to ethnic tensions.
swap.clue: The creation of this line, named for a British diplomat, effectively created a buffer zone between Britain and Russia in Asia. This line forms the de facto border between Afghanistan and Pakistan.

question.leadin: A king from this city named Fromo Kesaro, or "Rome Caesar," commemorated his defeat of Yazid ibn Ziyad in his coinage.
question.text: Name this westernmost capital city home to a Turkic "Shahi" dynasty that expanded to Gandhara. The Turk Shahis likely used the "Bala Hissar" fort in this city, as did the later Hindu Shahis who lost to Mahmud of Ghazni.
question.clue: A government in this city was established through the Peshawar Accord after the fall of Mohammad Najibullah.

swap.text: The destination of Younghusband's expedition was this region. Following the expedition, the Convention of Lhasa, signed in this region, allowed British trade in Yatung, Gyantse and Gartok.
swap.answerHtml: Tibet [or Xīzàng or Zàng or Böd or Poi ; do NOT accept or prompt on ‘Tibet Autonomous Region’ or ‘Xīzàng Zìzhìqū’]
swap.clue: Songtsan Gampo founded an empire in this region, later home to a line of religious leaders begun by Gendun Drup.

question.leadin: One ruler of this city sentenced two British diplomats to its prison's infamous "bug pit" after they tried to ride into his palace on horseback and arrived without a gift for him.
question.text: Name this city, the capital of an emirate that lost control of nearby Samarkand when it was attacked by Russia along with the neighboring Khiva and Kokand khanates.
question.clue: A group modelled off the Young Turks invited the Soviet conquest of this city and was given prominent leadership positions in the short-lived Soviet republic centered on this city.

swap.text: This so-called "Stalin of Mongolia" sought to reunite Outer and Inner Mongolia, but was thwarted by the real Stalin. He served as leader of Mongolia from 1939 to 1952.
swap.clue: With Shtern and Zukhov, this man commanded the winning side at the Battle of Khalkin Gol.

question.text: The author of History of the Hind, al-Biruni, traveled to India with the invading forces of Mahmud-i Zabuli, the first Sultan of this Turkic empire which broke off from the Samanids.
question.answerHtml: the Ghaznavid Empire [or Ghaznaviyan; Mahmud’s father Sabuktigin founded the dynasty but Mahmud was the first to call it a Sultanate]
question.clue: This empire whose first leader, Sabuktigin, was a slave before being promoted by Alptigin.

swap.leadin: An autocratic leader with this surname was buried in a mass grave outside the enormous Pul-e-Charkhi prison complex, whose construction he had ordered.
swap.text: Give this surname of Afghanistan's first President, who was executed during the Saur Revolution. That leader, Daoud, deposed King Zahir Shah, who had considered uniting Afghanistan with Pakistan per a proposal from a different president with this surname, Ayub.
swap.clue: One of these figures destroyed the Khwarezmian cities of Urgench and Samarkand and established his capital at Karakorum.

question.leadin: Boris Yeltsin once got so drunk that at a 1992 state dinner, he took a pair of wooden spoons and began drumming a tune on this leader's bald head.
question.text: Name this Central Asian leader, whose son Aidar married Nursultan Nazarbayev's daughter Aliya. The youth movement KelKel opposed this distinctively-eyebrowed, corrupt authoritarian, and helped pressure his resignation in 2005 during the Tulip Revolution.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a land once ruled by the Shaybanids, FTPE.
swap.text: Islam Karimov was the first president of this present day nation, whose territory was carved up from the Khorezm and Bukhara People's Republics and later augmented by the former Kara-Kalpak Autonomous SSR when it was set up in its prior incarnation as a Soviet Socialist Republic.
swap.clue: In one event in this country, Chulpon Avenue was closed and hundred of people in Bobur Square were killed in a protest blamed on the Islamic group Akramia.
